quote: I neither want to die nor do I want to want to die; I want to live for ever and ever and ever.
source: Miguel de Unamuno, Tragic Sense of Life, chapter III, The Hunger of Immortality (trans. J. E. Crawford Flitch, 1921)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg ebook 14636, the Dover reprint (1954) of Crawford Flitch’s Macmillan translation of 1921, read in full text
evidence.edition: Tragic Sense of Life, trans. J. E. Crawford Flitch, Macmillan, London, 1921 (Dover unaltered republication, 1954)
evidence.locator: chapter III, The Hunger of Immortality, the paragraph beginning Faced with this risk

reason: The wording is exact in Flitch’s text, chapter III. It is the part after the semicolon of a sentence that opens I do not want to die, no; cutting there drops only the dash and the no, and the clause is a full thought that begins with a capital I on its own. Unamuno has no line yet this year.
